This comment makes the ordering explicit: the Q group is packed before the page's dense predicate. At 4 heads that was about 71 ns of wasted pack per token per KV head for a page that turns out partial; at 16 heads it's about 660 ns (see my note on the pack loop), and the dispatch test's partial-page section pins the order by requiring one pack and no kernel call. Was the order deliberate for a reason I'm missing? If not, could the pack move into `apply_page_tok` after `is_dense_amx_page` returns true, with the partial-page expectation changed to zero packs?

`s_pages` is default-constructed, so its rows are value-initialized: a 4 KB zero fill per dense page visit at kv_mul 16, right before the QK kernel overwrites every element. The tensor already has an `uninitialized` constructor for this.

```suggestion
      tensor<operation_kv_mul, page::page_size> s_pages{uninitialized};
```

I didn't check whether thin LTO removes the fill on its own; the tag makes it not matter.

Checked by: `sed -n 40,42p h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp` -> `tensor() : data() {}` and `sed -n 254,256p` -> `std::construct_at(&data)`; the kernel writes all `group_heads x 64` floats at `amx_attn.cpp:244-253`.

This comment says the CMake CI lane configures with the option on, but I can't find a lane that runs on PRs and does. `cmake-single-platform.yml` has only `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call` triggers, its sole caller is `publish-deb.yml` (schedule, tag push, dispatch), and `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` never sets `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH`. So at this head the kernel TU, the call sites and every test case this PR adds compile out in CI, and both AMX binaries run as their `SUCCEED` stubs.

Could we add `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON` to `cmake_args` in `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix`? The dispatch and pack cases run on any AVX-512 host, the kernel cases `SKIP`, and the binary still exits 0. body:
The 16-head pack is a scalar triple loop, and at the `-O3` the build uses it compiles to 512 `vpextrw` stores. On a Zen 4 that's about 660 ns per call against 71 ns for the 4-head instantiation, and it runs once per token per KV head before the dense predicate.

Not a blocker for this PR, but a vectorised version looks like a contained follow-up: per 32-dim step, load 16 rows of 16 dwords (one head each), run the 4-stage unpack/shuffle dword transpose, store 16 panel rows, and mask the stores to 4 columns for the 4-head instantiation.

Checked by: opcode census of `pack_q_group_128x4<16>` from `clang++-19 -std=c++23 -O3 -mamx-tile -mamx-bf16 -mavx512f … -S src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp` -> `instrs 1258 vpextrw 512`; micro-benchmark on an EPYC 9654 -> `pack<16> 660 ns/call, pack<4> 71 ns/call`.

Lanes 1..3 of this store are pure AVX-512, but the only test that exercises them is `check_qk<GROUP_HEADS_16>()`, which sits behind the AMX `SKIP` guard, and the helper lives in an anonymous namespace so no TU without `-mamx` can reach it. Because the binary still has two passing cases, Catch2 exits 0 when the kernel cases skip, so ctest and Slice report a pass on the avx512 runners and the new lanes have never run in CI.

Could we declare a host-testable `transpose_scores<group_heads>(const float* s_transposed, float* s, size_t stride)` covering stages 1-4 in the interface header, build it in a TU without `-mamx`, and add an ungated `[q_pack]`-style case for 4 and 16 heads against a scalar transpose? The CMake comment could then also say that ctest and Slice still see a pass when the kernel cases skip.

Checked by: `grep -n store_transposed_rows h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp` -> nothing; `sed -n 316,325p t/t_amx_numerics.cpp` -> the only `check_qk<GROUP_HEADS_16>()` call follows the `SKIP` guard, and `bin/slice:1208` maps exit 0 to passed.

While reviewing I tried to split this diff into steps that each land on their own, and this hunk is the one I'd been treating as inseparable from the templating. It isn't: extracting lane 0 into `store_transposed_rows` is behaviour-identical for 4 heads (the `<4>` instantiation compiles to the same 204 instructions as the base's non-template kernel at `-O3`, zero diff lines), and the WARN-to-SKIP change is two three-line guards with no other dependency. If this PR gets reshaped into commits for landing, those two could go first as pure refactors, with the templating as the third step.

Checked by: object compare of `qk_rowmajor_128x4<4>` at head against the base kernel at `-O3` -> `204` vs `204` instructions, `0` diff lines; `t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:317-319` and `330-332` are the guards.

Each lane recomputes stage 3 here, so the 16-head store emits 48 shuffle-class instructions where 32 would do: lanes 0 and 2 share `pair_sel = 0x88` and lanes 1 and 3 share `0xdd`, so stage 3 has only 16 distinct results across the four lanes and stage 4 needs 16 more.

Minor, and fine as a follow-up: one `k` loop computing `p_even/q_even` (0x88) and `p_odd/q_odd` (0xdd) once per `k`, then storing lanes 0..3 from those with `quad_sel` 0x88/0xdd.

Checked by: opcode census of `qk_rowmajor_128x4<16>` from the clang 19 assembly at `-O3` -> `vshuff64x2 40 vinsertf64x4 8` = 48.

Not about the code: in the PR body's merge-base table, the qwen3-4b / tp2 / 1024 row shows +0.56 TPS against a 0.33 band and is marked "beyond". That row uses default FPGA attention and the kv_mul-4 kernels are instruction-identical to the base, so no PR code is on its path, which means the band understates run-to-run noise. Could the body either add paired repetitions until the untouched rows fall inside their bands, or say that the rule gates losses only?

Checked by: `gh pr view 5022 --json body -q .body | grep "qwen3-4b / tp2 / 1024"` -> `| 133.61 (0.16) | 134.17 (0.15) | +0.56 / 0.33, beyond | +0.03% |`.

This first `static_assert` restates the `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` clause on the template, and its message claims a store limitation the lane ladder doesn't have: lines 244-253 store lanes 0..3 under `if constexpr (lanes > N)`, which handles 4, 8, 12 and 16. The real constraint is the one the next assert half-states, plus an upper bound.

Could we replace these two lines with the actual constraint and keep the `% 4` assert?

    static_assert(group_heads / ROWS_PER_LANE_4 <= TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4,
        "at most 4 stored lanes of 4 rows");

If a tripwire for new sizes is intended, one comment line saying so would make that clear.

Both are out of date now: the head commit message explains the guard move (it removes the "variable 'probe' is not needed" warning of the option-less build), and the Nix lane built and ran the OFF arm at the head, Build Tron job 117831672410 and Test host job 117835534166. Could the description cite those two jobs in the OFF row and mention the guard move?

Every section uses one KV head, so the pack base `q.data + kv_head * operation_kv_mul * head_size` is only ever evaluated with `kv_head == 0`. The "starts at the wrong head" failure this comment promises can't be observed: the fake copies the first `group_heads * 128` values linearly, so the base is `q.data` for any multiplier.

Could we add a section with `n_heads = 32`, `n_kv_heads = 2`, call with `kv_head` 1 and REQUIRE `probe.q[i] == expected[16 * 128 + i]`? If that's more fixture than it's worth, I'd reword this to "a pack that reads the group with the wrong start or stride".

One more note from trying to split this diff into landable steps, in case it gets split into commits: I sliced the final diff by hunk and the slices kept the final diff's hunk headers. This one is `@@ -131,7 +140,16 @@`, which against the merge base would be `@@ -131,7 +131,16 @@`, so none of my slices was actually a patch against its parent and I never proved any step builds alone. This section drives the real `apply_dense_amx_page` epilogue with 16 heads, but the assertions stop at call counts, group sizes, stats and the packed input. Nothing reads any head's `v_star`, `s_star` or `m_star` afterwards, so an epilogue that only merged 4 of the 16 heads would still pass.

The fakes zero their outputs, so the expected state is exact. Could we loop `offset < group_heads` after `apply_page_range`, read `token_scratchpad_ref_at<geometry>(…)[kv_head * group_heads + offset]`, and REQUIRE `is_valid_for(0)`, `s_star == float(page_size)`, `m_star == 0.f` and every `v_star` element `== 0.f`?

Checked by: `grep -c "v_star\|s_star\|m_star\|is_valid_for" t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp` -> `0`.

This PR adds `const_k_row_major_plane_view` and `const_v_vnni_plane_view` to the interface header, but the two fakes here and the numerics call at `t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:183` still spell out `const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>` and `v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, ...>`. Could we use the aliases at those three sites so the tests name the layout the way the kernel does?

Checked by: `grep -n "const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64\|v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64" t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp t/t_amx_numerics.cpp` -> `:272`, `:282`, `t_amx_numerics.cpp:183`.

The 16-head instantiation is only exercised on a full page; the partial-page and kill-switch sections above and below use the 4-head default. The dense predicate itself is group-size independent, so I don't expect a defect here, but the asymmetry means a 16-head regression on either of those arms wouldn't be seen. Could we add `exercise_page<host_bf16, GROUP_HEADS_16>(page_size - 1)` and `exercise_page<host_bf16, GROUP_HEADS_16>(page_size, false, false)` sections?

Checked by: `sed -n 296,313p t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp` -> only line 305 passes `GROUP_HEADS_16`; lines 301 and 312 use the default.

`check_pv` asserts only rows below `group_heads` of `o_amx`. A P-fill loop bound regressed to 16 rows would, in production, read 3 KB past the 4x64 `s_pages` buffer (16 x 64 x 4 bytes against 1024 allocated), but the garbage would land only in the output rows this loop never checks, so the test would pass.

Could we add, after the loop in the 4-head case, `for (qi = group_heads; qi < TILE_ROWS_16; ++qi) for (d …) REQUIRE(o_amx[qi * HEAD_SIZE_128 + d] == 0.f);`? Then a regressed bound shows up as nonzero garbage in those rows.

Checked by: `sed -n 274,299p t/t_amx_numerics.cpp` -> the only loop over `o_amx` is `for (size_t qi = 0; qi < group_heads; ++qi)`; `self_attention.hpp:1755` sizes `s_pages` at `operation_kv_mul` rows.

Both tests gained sections but `config/test-benchmarks.json` wasn't refreshed, and `bin/slice bench --check` only validates the platform block, duplicate names and coverage gaps, so it can't flag that. Could we run `bin/slice bench --update t_amx_numerics t_amx_dispatch_dtype` after `bin/slice route`? `t/AGENTS.md` asks for the refresh after adding or materially changing a test.

Checked by: `git log --oneline -1 -- config/test-benchmarks.json` -> `2734ac421c`, already an ancestor of the merge base.

Now that this test uses Catch2 `SKIP`, a filtered run such as `t_amx_numerics "[kv_data]"` on a non-AMX host skips every selected case, and Catch2 then exits 4 (`AllTestsSkippedExitCode`). The registration at `t/CMakeLists.txt:619` has no `SKIP_RETURN_CODE`, so ctest and Slice would report that as a failure. The unfiltered binary is fine because its two pack cases pass and the exit stays 0.

Could we register it the way the other skipping tests in that file are?

    add_catch_test(NAME t_amx_numerics LIBRARIES tron pos_fake
      PROPERTIES SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4 LABELS "fake;skip_return_code_4")

and refresh the registry afterwards.
